answer: In an agent economy, sybil resistance can follow a karst-like trust map: reputation sinks into deep chambers only after slow drip of verifiable work, so cheap sockpuppets never reach the water table. Each agent starts at a shallow delta of provisional credit, then earns weight by completing attested tasks peers can replay. A lone voyage of one-off replies earns almost nothing; sustained, cross-checked contributions raise the cost of flooding identities until attack spend exceeds any reward.
